stories.headline: Putin unveils a nuclear submarine armed with hypersonic missiles
body: Putin attended the handover of the nuclear-powered submarine Perm to Russia's navy.
Moscow says it is the first sub carrying Zircon hypersonic missiles.
Russia plans five more nuclear submarines by 2030.
stories.vc: New weapons can push NATO countries to spend more on defence.

stories.headline: Venezuela to repeal law that bars opposition figures from office
body: Venezuela will scrap a 2024 law that banned opposition figures who backed sanctions from holding office.
Critics said the law enabled political persecution.
It comes a month after opposition leader María Corina Machado returned home.
stories.vc: Political openings could ease sanctions and draw oil investment.

stories.headline: Pakistan, Turkiye and Saudi Arabia condemn Houthi attacks
body: Officials from the three Mecca defence pact countries met in Islamabad on Friday.
Pakistan and Turkiye pledged to help protect Saudi Arabia's security.
Under the pact, an attack on one member counts as an attack on all.
stories.vc: Wider alliances could raise the stakes of Gulf attacks on oil sites.

stories.headline: Sensex falls 989 points as IT stocks and HDFC Bank slide
body: The Sensex fell 1.17% to 83,339.26 and the Nifty closed at 25,607.20.
Profit-taking hit IT stocks like HCL Tech, Infosys and TCS, plus HDFC Bank.
Rising crude oil prices added to the pressure.
stories.joke: Two days up, one big step down.
stories.vc: Volatile markets test investors' nerves after a strong rally.

stories.headline: RBI eases a cash rule to free up over ₹40,000 crore for banks
body: The RBI cut banks' minimum daily cash reserve requirement from 99% to 90%.
It should release more than ₹40,000 crore for lending.
The change starts from the fortnight beginning December 1.
stories.joke: Banks get a little more pocket money.
stories.vc: More liquidity can help keep loan rates in check.

stories.headline: Global fashion brands shift orders from Bangladesh to India
body: Brands like Zara and H&M moved about $254 million of orders out of Bangladesh between November 1 and 18, factory owners say.
That's nearly a tenth of monthly orders.
Most went to India, as unrest and rising costs hit Bangladesh.
stories.joke: Made in India, by popular demand.
stories.vc: More orders could boost jobs in India's garment hubs.

stories.headline: Haleon in talks to buy control of HealthKart
body: UK consumer health giant Haleon is in early talks to take a controlling stake in HealthKart at $1.2–1.4 billion, reports say.
HealthKart owns brands like MuscleBlaze, HK Vitals and Gritzo.
The startup had been weighing an IPO. (No new Unhedged episode, so this is Inc42's report.)
stories.joke: Protein shakes, now with a British accent.
stories.vc: A sale could give HealthKart's backers an exit without an IPO.

stories.headline: Trump faces Republican backlash over Nvidia CEO's return
body: Trump said he personally contacted Nvidia's board and 'convinced' it to bring back Jensen Huang.
Few Republicans backed him; some former officials warn it could hurt him with his base.
(Axios Pro Rata had nothing checkable, so this is Al Jazeera's report.)
stories.joke: Board meetings, now a political sport.
stories.vc: Political involvement adds governance risk for Nvidia investors.

stories.headline: IBM stops US visa sponsorship for most consulting roles
body: IBM will stop sponsoring US visas and green cards for most roles in its consulting arm.
The unit is its biggest, with over 150,000 employees.
Affected staff may be offered overseas moves or severance. (No new Stratechery post, so this is The Hindu's report.)
stories.vc: Fewer visas could shift more consulting work to India.

stories.headline: Volkswagen says Mercedes and BMW import parts the same way in its India tax fight
body: Volkswagen told an Indian court it was wrongly singled out over a $1.2 billion tax demand.
Authorities say it imported car kits as parts to pay 10% duty instead of about 30%.
VW says Mercedes-Benz, BMW and Kia do the same. (No Economist piece was readable, so this is a Reuters report via The Hindu.)
stories.joke: If I'm in trouble, so are my neighbours.
stories.vc: The case could change import costs for all foreign carmakers in India.

stories.headline: Dunzo co-founder Kabeer Biswas' AI startup M raises $9M
body: Kabeer Biswas' AI startup M raised $9 million in a round led by RTP Global, sources told Inc42.
Existing investors Peak XV Partners and Blume Ventures also put in more.
(TechCrunch Venture had no fresh deal over the US holiday, so this is Inc42's report.)
stories.joke: Founder's second act: one letter long.
stories.vc: Repeat founders still attract early-stage money in Indian AI.

stories.headline: Gaza's widows raise families alone in tents
body: More than 86,000 households in Gaza are now headed by women, UN Women says.
That's nearly one in four, up from one in nine before the war.
Widows haul water, find shelter and try to keep children in school.
stories.vc: Women heading households need income support and safe work.

stories.headline: A Samarkand shelter helps women escape violence
body: The Rahmdillik ('Compassion') crisis centre in Samarkand shelters women fleeing violence.
Surgeon Bibisora Oripova opened it in 1996 after treating burned women in hospital.
It now offers rooms and a sewing workshop.
stories.vc: Skills training helps survivors earn and stay independent.

stories.statLabel: years of abuse in the Mazan case
stories.headline: Gisèle Pelicot's son urges men to speak up against sexual violence
body: David Pelicot spoke at the UN about the silence of men after the Mazan rape trial.
He noticed almost all support for his mother came from women.
He says not being violent is 'the bare minimum'.
stories.vc: Changing men's attitudes is key to safer workplaces and homes.

stories.headline: High Court sets deadlines to fix AIIMS Deoghar's infrastructure
body: The Jharkhand High Court ordered the Centre and state to finish long-pending works at AIIMS Deoghar.
Deadlines cover electricity, water, fire safety, roads and land transfers.
The court said working tertiary care is a constitutional duty.
stories.joke: Deadlines: the cure for slow construction.
stories.vc: A fully working AIIMS cuts long trips to big-city hospitals.

stories.headline: Delhi plans an app to show free hospital beds for poorer patients
body: Delhi plans an app showing vacant EWS beds, including ICU beds, at private hospitals.
About 3,235 EWS patients were treated free each day between April 2025 and October 2026.
A live web portal already exists.
stories.vc: Better information makes free private beds actually usable.

stories.statLabel: a month Max doctors spend in Dubai
stories.headline: Max Healthcare doctors to operate at a Dubai hospital
body: Max Healthcare signed a deal with Clemenceau Medical Centre Hospital in Dubai.
Its orthopaedic and urology specialists will visit three days a month for consultations and surgeries.
They will also do robotic surgeries there.
stories.vc: Overseas partnerships give Indian hospital chains new revenue.

stories.headline: Kalshi avoids an immediate New York shutdown, for now
body: Kalshi won a reprieve after a November 23 hearing in New York's case against it.
New York says Kalshi runs illegal gambling; the CFTC says New York wants it out of business.
The fight over whether prediction markets are gambling or derivatives continues.
stories.joke: Bet on the outcome? Probably not legal in New York.
stories.vc: The ruling will shape how prediction markets are regulated in the US.

stories.headline: Broker Vantage doubles leverage on 24/7 gold trading to 1:1000
body: Offshore broker Vantage Markets raised maximum leverage on small 24/7 gold CFD positions from 1:500 to 1:1000.
It's the second increase since the product launched in July.
Offshore brokers use high leverage to attract small retail accounts.
stories.vc: High leverage magnifies losses for small traders.

stories.headline: Explainer: What is leverage?
body: Imagine you have ₹10, and a friend lends you ₹990 to buy ₹1,000 worth of sweets to resell.
If prices rise a little, you make a big profit on your tiny ₹10. If they fall a little, your ₹10 vanishes fast.
Borrowing to trade bigger like this is called leverage.
This week, broker Vantage raised leverage on its 24/7 gold trades to 1:1000 for small positions.
Leverage makes small price moves feel huge, both ways.
stories.vc: Leverage cuts both ways.

stories.headline: Antonelli tops both Qatar GP practice sessions for Mercedes
body: Kimi Antonelli swept Friday practice in Qatar, with George Russell second for Mercedes.
Two red flags interrupted FP2 after Leclerc spun and Gasly beached his Alpine.
Hamilton stopped late with an apparent power unit shutdown.
stories.joke: Mercedes: fastest on Friday, hoping for Sunday.
stories.vc: A late-season Mercedes surge boosts its sponsor story for 2027.
